qt: to the Commission Gianantonio Da Re (ID) Subject:

According to the Italian Association of Medical Oncology (Associazione Italiana Oncologia Medica – AIOM), there has been a rapid growth in the incidence of cancer over the last 20 years, especially among younger age groups and the under-50s. According to the AIOM report, the number of cancer cases in Italy has increased by over 18 000 in the last three years alone, to stand at 395 000, with the increase applying to both sexes, especially after the pandemic. The study clearly shows that the actual number of deaths due to cancer has decreased over the years, but that the number of cases among the under-50s rose by 80 % from 1990 to 2019. In view of the above, can the Commission clearly state whether it plans to increase funding and grants for scientific research into curbing the incidence of cancer?
at: (English version) to the Commission Gianantonio Da Re (ID) (2 February 2024) Subject: Increase in cancer cases among the younger sections of the European population According to the Italian Association of Medical Oncology (Associazione Italiana Oncologia Medica — AIOM), there has been a rapid growth in the incidence of cancer over the last 20 years, especially among younger age groups and the under-50s. According to the AIOM report, the number of cancer cases in Italy has increased by over 18 000 in the last three years alone, to stand at 395 000, with the increase applying to both sexes, especially after the pandemic. The study clearly shows that the actual number of deaths due to cancer has decreased over the years, but that the number of cases among the under-50s rose by 80% from 1990 to 2019. In view of the above, can the Commission clearly state whether it plans to increase funding and grants for scientific research into curbing the incidence of cancer? (3 April 2024) The Horizon Europe Cancer Mission (1) was established in 2021 with the ambition ‘to improve the lives of more than 3 million people by 2030, through prevention, cure and for those affected by cancer including their families, to live longer and better’. Together with Europe’s Beating Cancer Plan (2), the Mission aims to ensure that new evidence generated through Research & Innovation (R&I) is systematically translated into concrete solutions for patients and to assist Member States in delivering efficient cancer control strategies. Between 2021-2023, the Cancer Mission committed EUR 360 million to supporting 46 new projects in the areas of understanding, prevention screening and early detection, diagnosis and treatment and quality of life, addressing also cancer in children, adolescents and young adults. Over the same period, under Horizon Europe (3), funding for cancer R&I totalled EUR 1.4 billion, exploiting also synergies established with other initiatives. Cancer research will continue to be prioritised over the next years, in line with the ambitious goals set in the Cancer Mission Implementation plan (4). This includes also research aiming to clarify the potential contribution of environmental risk factors to the development of cancer in the younger age groups.
